title: Probing-based microbatch trimming and opportunistic GPU slab reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-QPS ingress scenarios intermittently trigger aggressive microbatch admission and long-lived KV cache retention, causing GPU slab fragmentation and sustained headroom starvation. This ticket implements a lightweight probing mechanism to identify safely-trimmable microbatches and an opportunistic GPU slab reclamation path that runs during low-utilization micro-windows. The goal is to reduce tail latency spike frequency and improve sustained throughput without regressing p50 latency.
acceptance_criteria: Tail-99 latency for generation requests under synthetic spike workload (3x baseline QPS for 60s bursts) reduced by >= 20% compared to current main branch
Mean GPU free slab reclaim cycles do not add >1.5ms p50 overhead to normal requests when reclamation runs during micro-windows
No increase in token-generation error rate (model failures) beyond 0.1% absolute
Feature gated behind 'probe_trim_reclaim' and launchable via runtime flag; default off for Dedicated customers until rollout
End-to-end telemetry dashboards (reclaims/sec, reclaimed_bytes, probe_success_rate, blocked_admissions) created in Console and linked from ticket
design_notes: Probing component: on first admission to a newly formed microbatch group, attach a 1–2 token lightweight synthetic probe request (no model eval) to measure KV residency and memory touch patterns; probe runs inline but marked low-priority so it can be preempted

Trim policy: if probe indicates >70% of KV entries in the group are cold (no recent access bits) and microbatch age > 120ms, mark group as 'elective-trim' and allow deterministic early completion via a fast-path that reuses partial KV state

Reclamation windowing: maintain an opportunistic reclamation loop that triggers when GPU utilization < 45% for >= 15ms and there is at least one elective-trim candidate; reclamation coalesces small free regions into slab-sized chunks to avoid fragmentation
Safety: all trims must preserve correct KV lane invariants; trimmed groups can be rehydrated from backing store or fallback to full-model path if misses occur

Backpressure integration: when reclamation cannot keep up and currently free slabs < threshold, emit a soft backpressure signal that increases microbatch admission timeout progressively rather than hard rejections
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype probe inserter in local scheduler (1 week) — expose probe config via runtime flag
Bench: run microbench harness against Llama-2-13B-ggml under controlled KV patterns to tune thresholds (2 weeks)
Engine: add elective-trim fast-path with safe rehydration fallback, unit tests for KV invariants (1.5 weeks)
Reclaim: implement opportunistic slab coalescer + small defragmentation routine in runtime allocator (1.5 weeks)
Telemetry: add metrics (probe_success_rate, elective_trims, reclaimed_bytes, reclaim_latency, soft_backpressure_events) and Console panels (2 days)
Rollout: feature-flagged Canary on non-critical region, monitor, gradual ramp (2 weeks)
measurement_plan: Synthetic load: 3x/5x baseline QPS bursts for 60–120s with mixed short/long sequences; measure p50/p90/p99/gen latency, token/s throughput, and GPU memory fragmentation histogram
Canary: sample 1% of traffic in us-west-2 on Dedicated pools for 48h; compare to control using traffic shadowing
Real-user signals: monitor rate of reclamation-induced fallbacks and increase in model inference errors; alert if >0.1% or if reclaimed_bytes growth stalls >10 minutes
Cost telemetry: track any increase in per-token latency that might affect billing and summarize expected performance delta for customers
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal nightly cluster with flag enabled for stress tests and perf validation
Canary: 1% traffic in us-west-2 Dedicated, observe 48h, roll back on high error or tail regressions
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 2–3 weeks with automated rollback thresholds
Customer opt-in: Keep feature off for Hosted API by default; early enterprise customers can opt into Private/Dedicated beta via support ticket
risks: Incorrect probe heuristics could misclassify hot KV entries as cold leading to elevated model latency due to rehydration misses
Reclamation may cause contention with normal allocations if the opportunistic windowing is too aggressive
Telemetery volume growth from probes/reclaims could inflate metrics costs; keep probe sampling low and aggregated
Edge cases for multi-tenant Dedicated pools: tenant A reclamation may affect tenant B tail behavior — mitigate via per-tenant accounting
